documents.title: Press Release - CPCL Financial Performance For The Quarter And Half Year Ended 30.09.2026
Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Press Release / Media Release
Audited Financial Results For The Quarter And Half Year Ended 30.09.2026

analysis.summary: Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited reported its financial and operational performance for Q4 and FY26, achieving a highest-ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT and record production across several value-added products. Management highlighted strong operational efficiencies, improved distillate yields, and a robust financial position with significantly reduced leverage. The company also announced major ongoing and upcoming capital expenditure plans, including Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS projects and retail expansion. Despite macroeconomic and geopolitical volatility affecting crude sourcing, management expressed confidence in sustaining long-term operational and financial momentum. Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL) reported its financial and operational performance for Q4 and FY25, highlighting resilient physical performance despite scheduled maintenance shutdowns.

demand_outlook.claim: Motor Spirit (MS) in the southern market faces a clear shortfall where production is less than demand.
demand_outlook.quote: MS in southern market, there is a clear shortfall so, the production is less than demand.

capex_expansion.claim: The company has all approvals in place for the Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project, and execution has started in full swing.
capex_expansion.quote: Some of the important projects that we'll be taking up is Group 2, Group 3 LOBS for which all approvals are in place and the project execution has started in full swing.

capex_expansion.claim: The retail outlet endeavor involving 300 licenses has started, and commissioning will occur during the financial year.
capex_expansion.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started. And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

capex_expansion.claim: The Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project is budgeted at INR1,600 crores and the retail outlet project at INR400 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: LOBS project, Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project is INR1,600 crores. The retail outlet project is INR400 crores.

capex_expansion.claim: The revised capital cost for the CBR refinery project stands at Rs. 36,354 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: The revised capital cost is at Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian oil respectively.

capex_expansion.claim: The new refinery capacity is 9 million metric tons with a petrochemical intensity of 6% for polypropylene.
capex_expansion.quote: The new refinery capital cost is Rs 36,000 Crore approximately, 9 million metric ton capacity and petrochemical intensity of 6% and which is PP, polypropylene.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL spent Rs. 673 crores as capex for the current financial year.
capex_expansion.quote: On the CAPEX front, in the current year, we have spent Rs. 673 crores as CAPEX for the current year.

margins_costs.claim: The gross refining margin for quarter 4 was $13.75 per barrel compared to the Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for quarter 4 was $13.75 barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel, which again reiterates that all these efficiencies are constant, continuous and are being sustained over each period.

margins_costs.claim: The core GRM for the fourth quarter was $10.3 per barrel.
Foreign exchange loss for the quarter was approximately INR200 crores and around INR350 crores for the full year.
margins_costs.quote: For the quarter, it would be for the quarter, it is approximately INR 200 crores,. And for the whole year, it will be around INR350 crores.

margins_costs.claim: The Gross Refining Margin (GRM) for FY 2024-25 was $4.22 per barrel compared to $8.64 per barrel in the previous year.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for 2024-25 for a full year basis is $4.22 per barrel as compared to the previous year $8.64 per barrel, but if you compare it to Singapore benchmark which was $3.79 per barrel in the current year, we have performed better.

margins_costs.claim: For Q4 FY25, the Gross Refining Margin was $6.22 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: On Quarter 4, our GRM was $6.22 per barrel.

margins_costs.claim: Inventory gain for Q4 FY25 was $0.66 per barrel, amounting to Rs. 125 crores.
margins_costs.quote: Yes, the inventory gain is not very significant for the quarter. It is only $ 0.66 per barrel. And in absolute rupee terms, it is Rs. 125 crores only.

margins_costs.claim: Operating expenditure was 1,085 crore in 2022-23, 1,215 crore in 2023-24, and 945 crore in 9M 2024-25.
CPCL reported GRM was $11.91/bbl in 2022-23, $8.64/bbl in 2023-24, and $3.40/bbl in 9M 2024-25.
Interest expenses stood at 330 crore in 2022-23, 223 crore in 2023-24, and 165 crore in 9M 2024-25.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 million metric tons, equivalent to 112% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, million metric ton, which equivalents to 112% of installed capacity, breaking records of our previous best of 11.64 MMT achieved in financial year 2023-'24.

orders_capacity.claim: In quarter 4, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is 111% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: In quarter 4 of the current financial year, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is also 111% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: The company reached a highest ever distillate yield of 79.1% during the year.
orders_capacity.quote: Further, highest ever distillate yield of 79.1%, beating our previous record of 77.6% set in 2019-'20 was also achieved during this year.

orders_capacity.claim: The capacity of pharma-grade Hexane was doubled from 30 to 60.
orders_capacity.quote: It was 30, now the capacity is 60.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT, which is 99.5% of its installed capacity during the year.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT, equivalent to 99.5% of our installed capacity and this must be seen with respect to the turnaround that has happened during the year

orders_capacity.claim: Crude throughput for Quarter 4 was 2.974 MMT, representing 113% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: coming on to Quarter 4, the crude throughput was 2.974, which is 113% of installed capacity.

capital_allocation.claim: Gross borrowings stand at INR1,900 crores and net borrowings are at INR973 crores.
capital_allocation.quote: On a gross basis, the borrowings are INR1,900 crores, but on a net basis, it is less than INR1,000 crores, to be precise, INR973 crores.

capital_allocation.claim: Capex for the current year was INR856 crores compared to INR673 crores in the previous year.
capital_allocation.quote: During the current year, the capex was INR856 crores as compared to INR673 crores in the previous year.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share, representing 50% of the face value.
capital_allocation.quote: With the above, the Board has also recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share that is 50% of face value for the current year and as we all know, this is subject to approval at AGM, which will happen in the due course.

capital_allocation.claim: Total absolute debt as of March 31, 2025, stands at Rs. 3,100 crores.
capital_allocation.quote: At an absolute level, the debt stands at Rs. 3,100 crores as compared to Rs. 2,762 crores as on March 31, 2024.

capital_allocation.claim: Net worth as of March 31, 2025, is Rs. 7,939 crores.
capital_allocation.quote: Net worth is at Rs. 7,939 crores as on March 31, 2025.

risks_headwinds.claim: Uncertainties due to logistical constraints and volatility of crude oil prices pose ongoing challenges.
risks_headwinds.quote: Now with all this, I would like to say the uncertainties due to logistical constraints, volatility of crude oil prices do pose challenges.

risks_headwinds.claim: Uncertainties due to the volatility of crude prices pose a challenge for the company.
risks_headwinds.quote: Finally, the uncertainties due to volatility of crude prices do pose a challenge.

risks_headwinds.claim: Provision for contingent liabilities was 218 crore in 2022-23, 10 crore in 2023-24, and 9 crore in 9M 2024-25.
Exchange variation gain or loss was 523 crore in 2022-23, 72 crore in 2023-24, and 122 crore in 9M 2024-25.
CST under recovery was 463 crore in 2022-23, 361 crore in 2023-24, and 246 crore in 9M 2024-25.

management_commitments.claim: The INR2,000 crores capex for LOBS and retail outlets will happen over 2 to 3 years.
management_commitments.quote: This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years.

management_commitments.claim: Normal maintenance capex is assumed at another INR500 crores every year.
management_commitments.quote: Besides, every year, you can assume another INR500 crores is our normal capex.

management_commitments.claim: Maintenance capex for the next year is expected to be in the range of Rs. 200 to Rs. 250 crores.
management_commitments.quote: The maintenance CAPEX will be at around Rs. 200-250 crore range and depending on value added projects approvals, the actual will be a little different.

management_commitments.claim: Without the LOBS project, maintenance capex for the next two years would be around Rs. 300 crores per year, and with the project, it would be around Rs. 700 to Rs. 800 crores per year.
management_commitments.quote: The normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores, maintenance CAPEX plus small regular CAPEX normally. And with this project, another Rs. 400 to Rs. 500 crores you can add for each of the year. So, without this project, about Rs. 300 crores per year. With this project, about Rs. 700 to Rs. 800 crores per year.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
